source.title: SuperBPE: Space Travel for Language Models
source.authors: Alisa Liu; J. Hayase; Valentin Hofmann; Sewoong Oh; Noah A. Smith; Ye-Jin Choi

record.tranche_reason: The study measures bits-per-byte loss across training-compute sweeps at two model-size baselines, but does not fit or evaluate the power-law forms in the claim.
record.gate_note: The downstream-task scores compare tokenizer choices rather than test downstream scaling predictability. They are not recorded as rows for V6. The tokenizer efficiency and inference-compute results likewise do not measure a claim version.
record.test_reason: This is a tokenizer paper: it compares SuperBPE with BPE at fixed compute. The scaling sweeps span only 0.5× to 4× the base token budget at two base sizes, and no power law is fitted, extrapolated or checked. Kaplan and Hoffmann are cited only to motivate token-to-parameter ratios (§B.4.2). All rows compare the study's own method with a baseline; none measures a claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record overweights the appendix scaling results. The main conclusion: SuperBPE tokenizers improve downstream performance (+4.0% average over 30 tasks at 8B, fixed train compute) and cut inference compute by about 27%. Scaling experiments show matched-inference-compute SuperBPE gives lower BPB at all tested budgets, while matched-parameter SuperBPE helps only when under-trained. No conclusion is drawn about power laws.
record.recipe_differences: This study changes tokenization and compares BPB across training budgets and model sizes; it does not reproduce the scaling-law fitting procedure or test the original fitted laws.
record.method_sensitivity: The relative BPB ranking changes with tokenizer comparison (matching parameter count versus matching inference compute) and training regime (under-trained versus over-trained); the reported gaps also change when model size and training tokens are scaled together.

fits_no_version.finding: Tokenizer choice shifts BPB-vs-compute curves. Matched-parameter SuperBPE beats BPE when under-trained but loses when over-trained, and the gaps shrink when model size and tokens are scaled together. At 8B, BPB ranking and downstream ranking disagree.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Tokenizer efficiency changes the loss-versus-compute trade-off and the loss-to-downstream mapping. Scaling comparisons across tokenizers are therefore not equivalent.

record.problems: The scaling evidence is limited to 680M and 1.9B baseline sizes and the tested training budgets; BPB values for the scaling sweeps are presented in plots rather than reported numerically in the text. The study does not fit power laws or report uncertainty for these comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No reported results bearing on the claim were left out.

untested.parts: No power-law fit. Training budgets span under one order of magnitude per size.
The shape is scaled uniformly by design; its effect is not measured.
The downstream comparison is between tokenizers. Authors note BPB and task rankings disagree, but this is not a scaling test.
No exponents are fitted, so their dependence on setup is not tested.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's relation 'tests' and tranche T2 are not supported. All rows are comparisons of the study's own tokenizer against BPE, so they are relinked to none. The BPE baseline curves fall with compute, but only over a narrow range and without any fit.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not fit power laws or test exponents, several-orders-of-magnitude behavior, or independent sweeps of parameters, tokens, and compute with the other factors non-bottlenecking.

conditions.value: train tokens and parameters scaled proportionately
BPE versus SuperBPE matched-parameter and inference-compute settings

rows.value: The gap between the settings decreases with scale; across the experiments, matching inference compute is almost universally best, while matching parameter count is generally worse than BPE except in the under-trained regime.
rows.note: The prose reports aggregate trends; it does not give numerical BPB values or fit a power law.
rows.check: Aggregate tokenizer-gap trends with scale. The gap between settings is the measure, not the loss-scaling form.
